sampling_model.design: I.i.d. superpopulation sampling from a fixed finite-stratum law.
sampling_model.treatment: The latent dose \(A_i\) is observed only through \(S_{i1}=A_i+U_{i1}\) and \(S_{i2}=A_i+U_{i2}\); the errors are independent, nonidentically distributed, potentially asymmetric, and may have characteristic-function zero sets.
sampling_model.overlap: The finite strata have masses at least \(p_{\min}\), and \(f_x(a)\ge\kappa\) on \(I\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The probability and signed marked channels are controlled by continuous integrated empirical contrasts on \(\mathcal C_*\). Entire-transform continuation and Sobolev recovery are profiled jointly, and band endpoints are measurable extrema over the exact compact profile.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The compact-support blind-replicate density estimator attains squared \(L^2\) risk of order \((\log\log n/\log n)^{2\beta}\), with a matching density lower bound.
The known-error continuous-treatment estimator admits pointwise asymptotic inference for the ADRF.

Theorems S11 and S12 give a uniform-in-treatment asymptotically linear representation and multiplier-bootstrap inference for the ADRF when the continuous treatment is observed without measurement error.
A latent-variable variational framework estimates a continuous-treatment ADRF under measurement error with neural density models.
Inverting finite complex Kotlarski moment tests gives a uniformly size-controlled latent-density confidence band without imposing completeness.
A multiplier-bootstrap density band is uniformly valid when the unknown error law is learned from auxiliary data or symmetric repeated measurements.
Wavelet deconvolution estimators attain minimax sup-norm density rates under a known convolution operator.
Testing affinity yields lower bounds on confidence-band width over nonparametric function classes.
Under weak unconfoundedness and positivity, the error-free ADRF is identified by the continuous-treatment g-formula.

body.tldr: The observed law supplies an unmarked probability channel and an outcome-marked signed channel. Continuous integrated control on the moment-protected square, quantitative analytic continuation, and Sobolev recovery yield a theoretical exact-profile simultaneous ADRF band with minimax expected maximal width \(r_n\asymp(\log\log n/\log n)^{\beta-1/2}\) for every fixed \(\beta>1/2\). Compactness and measurable-extremum arguments make the exact-profile endpoints well defined. A fixed-density Bernoulli marked experiment based on a weighted Jacobi packet and fixed asymmetric sinc-fourth-mixture errors supplies the matching lower bound.

project_justification.gap: Existing error-free ADRF work gives uniform inference, known-error methods give pointwise ADRF inference, and blind repeated-measurement work treats an unmarked density. None combines an honest whole-curve ADRF band, a sharp expected-width modulus, and a fixed-nuisance marked converse when two replicate errors are unknown, nonidentical, asymmetric, and allowed spectral zeros.
project_justification.niche: Compact dose support makes both latent transforms entire, while the common error second-moment radius supplies a uniformly nonvanishing protected neighborhood. The inferential object is a paired nonlinear quotient, and the band is formed by measurable extrema over the exact compact continuous-channel profile.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the paired protected inverse at exponent \(\beta-1/2\), embeds it in a continuously constrained exact confidence profile, and bounds the profile diameter at the matching rate. A Bernoulli marked weighted-Jacobi construction with fixed asymmetric sinc-fourth-mixture errors leaves the unmarked replicate law fixed and matches the upper rate.

body.related_work: Colangelo and Lee (2025), especially Supplementary Theorems S11 and S12, are the closest uniform-in-treatment ADRF comparator, but treatment is observed without error. Huang and Zhang (2023) derive pointwise ADRF inference with a known error transform. Gao, Bondell, Huang, and Gong (2024) estimate a latent-treatment ADRF through a variational neural model without a blind-replicate honest-band theorem. Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehericy (2025) provide the closest blind-replicate method exemplar through a continuous integrated analytic-polynomial contrast and compact-support density rates; the present lower experiment instead uses a weighted Jacobi reproducing-kernel packet in the Bernoulli marked channel together with two fixed nonidentical asymmetric mixtures of shifted and scaled sinc-fourth densities. Kato, Sasaki, and Ura (2021) invert complex Kotlarski moment tests for an unmarked density. Kato and Sasaki (2018, 2019) study density and errors-in-variables regression bands under auxiliary, symmetric, or conventional spectral information, while Neumann (2007) motivates integrated characteristic-function coordinates. Evdokimov and White (2012) weaken Kotlarski identification conditions under mutual independence and a location normalization by permitting specified characteristic-function zeros, but provide neither marked-ADRF inference nor an honest-band width rate. Belomestny and Goldenshluger (2021) obtain pointwise and \(L^2\) density-deconvolution rates with a known error distribution whose characteristic function may vanish, under analytic zero-structure and signal moment conditions; their fixed-operator density problem does not cover blind paired channels, a marked quotient, or simultaneous ADRF bands. Babii (2020) constructs honest uniform confidence sets with controlled expected diameter for Tikhonov-regularized linear ill-posed models using concentration and bootstrap arguments, whereas the present operator is blind and bilinear and its matching lower bound fixes all unmarked nuisances. Bull (2012) shows that honest adaptation across Hölder smoothness classes in direct density, regression, and white-noise bands requires self-similarity; the present frontier fixes \(\beta>1/2\), claims no smoothness adaptation, and derives a different logarithmic rate from blind analytic continuation. Lounici and Nickl (2011), Genovese and Wasserman (2008), and Low (1997) inform sup-norm recovery and confidence-band lower reductions. These are informed-by comparisons; the separate error-free reduction is the only equivalence claim.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The compactness and measurable-extremum proof is non-effective. Under the unchanged Sobolev and second-moment model, a terminating finitely checkable witness cover of the exact profile, with rigorously negligible endpoint error and without an oracle decision of abstract decoder nonemptiness, remains open as \(\text{oeq:finite-profile-certification}\). Thus the delivered frontier is a statistical existence and exact-profile result, not an effective numerical certification theorem. On the converse side, the weighted Jacobi packet must preserve Bernoulli range, Sobolev slack, fixed nuisances, and product-law affinity.
body.honest_scope: The frontier fixes \(\beta>1/2\), the support interval, Sobolev radii, overlap constants, outcome bound, and error second-moment radius. Error laws remain unknown, nonidentical, asymmetric, and may have zeros outside the protected neighborhood. Band endpoints are exact extrema of the continuous integrated profile. Adaptation to unknown smoothness or drifting channel severity is outside the theorem. The error-free reduction remains a separate specialization.
